title: Design System: Anubhav Mishra · LLM systems, measured

themes.mechanism: CSS custom properties on :root (--paper, --ink, --muted, --rule, --hair, --seal, --on-seal, --on-ink). Dark values apply under :root[data-theme='dark'] or prefers-color-scheme: dark without data-theme='light'. A pre-paint inline script restores the saved choice from localStorage.

display.purpose: The subject's name only; Archivo 800 at width 116%.

statement.purpose: The single claim under test; condensed to width 94%, max 27ch.

headline.purpose: Section and contact headings; 2rem stepping to 2.5rem at md.

document-title.purpose: The certificate's name in the top rule; uppercase, widely tracked, width 125%; one per page.

body.purpose: Bullets, achievements, skills, result captions; max 68-70ch.

data.purpose: Result readings; Red Hat Mono, tabular, slashed zero; denominator in faded ink.

label.purpose: Field labels and list group names (uppercase); margin metadata, conditions and run readings at the same size in sentence case.

borders.name: section-rule
borders.purpose: Opens the header and every section.

borders.name: field-rule
borders.purpose: Frames link cells, buttons, the run switch, the photo, and starts lists.

borders.name: record-rule
borders.purpose: Separates project records, the margin column edge, the statement divider.

motion.name: print-cell

motion.purpose: Result cells re-print when the run switch changes. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.purpose: Anchor navigation; only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

narrative.overview:
The page is a calibration certificate. Every claim is a field on a ruled form, every number states the conditions it was measured under, and the evidence is a strip of square pass/fail cells printed in one flat green. The sheet is cool paper with near-black ink rules; the only colour that is not ink is the seal.

Density is that of a test report: a fixed margin column carries record metadata in small mono type, a label column names each field, and the value column holds the content. Heavy, expanded Archivo carries the fields that must be read from across a room (the subject's name, section headings); Red Hat Mono carries the data. Dark mode is not a different design, it is the same certificate laid on a lightbox: ink ground, paper-white type, seal green lifted for luminance.

Nothing floats. There are no shadows, no radii on rectangles, no gradients, no tints. Depth and grouping come from rule weight alone (2px ink between sections, 1px ink around fields, hairlines between rows). The one curved object is the seal itself, a rotated circular stamp, which is why it reads as a stamp.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled field grid: margin column | label column | value, collapsing to stacked label-over-value on narrow screens.
One accent, seal green, printed flat at full strength; never tinted, never a gradient.
Square corners everywhere except the circular seal.
Archivo on its width axis (94% to 125%) for fields and headings; Red Hat Mono, tabular and slashed-zero, for data, conditions, and record metadata.
Signature motion: the Before/After run switch re-prints every result cell, staggered, and snaps instantly under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Flat Seal Rule
rules.body: Seal green appears at 100% or not at all: no alpha, no tints, no gradients, no green-on-green. Hover and pressed states move between ink, hair, and seal; they never lighten the seal.

rules.name: The Green Means Passed Rule
rules.body: Seal green is reserved for measured success, the stamp, and interaction feedback (focus, hover, selection). It is never decoration, never a section fill, never a heading colour.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Red Hat Mono is for numbers, conditions, repository paths, email addresses, field labels, and record metadata. Prose, headings, and buttons are Archivo.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is set by weight and font-stretch together: expand (110% to 125%) for headings and the document title, condense (94%) for the long statement. Do not reach for a second display face.

rules.name: The Rule Weight Rule
rules.body: Structure is told by line weight: 2px ink opens the header and each section, 1px ink frames fields and starts lists, 1px ruling grey separates records, hairline separates rows. Pick the weight by structural level, not by taste.

rules.name: The Invert, Don't Lift Rule
rules.body: An active or primary element becomes a solid ink (or seal on hover) fill with paper type. Nothing rises, glows, or casts a shadow.

dos: Do set every claim as a field: a mono label in the label column, the value beside it, separated by rules.
Do state the conditions next to every number, in mono, in faded ink.
Do use seal green at full strength only, for passes, the stamp, focus, selection, and hover feedback.
Do keep every rectangle square (0px) and every icon a square-capped 1.6-stroke SVG.
Do choose rule weight by structural level: 2px ink for sections, 1px ink for fields and list tops, hairline for rows.
Do gate every movement behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; the cell re-print snaps when motion is reduced.
Do keep dark mode as the same sheet on a lightbox: swap the token values, never the layout or the accent's role.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients, glows, or tinted/transparent seal green.
Don't round rectangles; the circular seal is the only curve.
Don't set prose, headings, or buttons in Red Hat Mono, or bring in a second display face.
Don't put small uppercase labels above headings; labels live in the label or margin column beside their value.
Don't introduce a second accent colour or use green for anything that is not a pass, the stamp, or interaction feedback.
Don't use Unicode glyphs as icons.
Don't wrap content in cards; group with rules.
